html:
The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) joined Africa's independent states from 1963 to 2002, set up to end colonial rule and defend its members' independence. It was founded in Addis Ababa, hosted by Haile Selassie.

Kwame Nkrumah wanted a single African government, but most leaders preferred a loose club of sovereign states, and they won. In 1964 the OAU agreed that the new states would keep their colonial borders.

Its main work was helping liberation movements against Portuguese rule, white Rhodesia and apartheid. Its weakness was silence about abuses at home: Idi Amin served as its chairman. It adopted the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights in 1981, and Thomas Sankara used its 1987 summit to urge Africa not to pay its debts. The African Union replaced it in 2002.
sum: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) joined Africa's independent states from 1963 to 2002, set up to end colonial rule and defend its members' independence. It was founded in Addis Ababa, hosted by Haile Selassie.
